architectureStages.title: Central management

caseStudy.headline: Factory signals. One operational view.
caseStudy.problem: Factory equipment exposes data through different interfaces, leaving machine events and sensor readings distributed across the production floor. A central system needs to identify the source, understand the message type and retain the event history.
caseStudy.solution: A layered system connects equipment-specific interfaces to ESP32 field nodes and a central SBC. LoRa carries structured notifications; the main system manages identities, routes notifications to subscribed nodes and makes journaled records accessible on the local network.

capabilities.title: Modular equipment interfaces
capabilities.detail: Equipment-specific adapters communicate with field nodes through I2C or UART, keeping machine integration separate from wireless transport.

capabilities.title: Distributed field nodes
capabilities.detail: ESP32-based nodes aggregate equipment notifications using C firmware and communicate with the main system over LoRa.

capabilities.title: Notification registry & routing
capabilities.detail: The main system assigns node and record identifiers, associates notification types with UUIDs, and records donor and subscriber relationships for message routing.

capabilities.title: Event history & local access
capabilities.detail: The central Go management layer journals notifications and exposes a local-network interface for reviewing machine events and sensor history.

workflow.name: Register
workflow.detail: The main system identifies each node and registers the notification types it produces or accepts.

workflow.name: Collect & transmit
workflow.detail: An equipment interface supplies a machine event or sensor reading to its node, which packages it as a LoRa notification.

workflow.name: Journal & route
workflow.detail: The main system stores the notification and forwards it to subscribed nodes where required.

workflow.name: Review
workflow.detail: Operators access the local-network interface to inspect the recorded event and its source.

caseStudy.example: A button event and a temperature reading illustrate the message path: each equipment interface produces its own notification type, the field node forwards it, and the main system records the event for review. This describes the system workflow rather than a live demonstration.
caseStudy.outcome: The completed company project brings equipment interfaces, distributed nodes and central management into a modular industrial automation system, with identifiable notifications, event history and local-network access.

faq.question: What does BGirgin Hardware focus on?
faq.answer: Hardware, embedded systems, robotics and industrial automation. Quadropod and Industrial LoRa Platform are the main products, supported by electronics, firmware and device software work.

faq.question: Can I buy a Quadropod robot today?
faq.answer: Quadropod is currently a development project, not an off-the-shelf robot. The available V0 evidence is an articulated leg CAD prototype. Physical validation and embedded control are planned.

faq.question: What is Industrial LoRa Platform?
faq.answer: A completed BGirgin Hardware company project for factory monitoring and automation. It combines modular equipment interfaces, ESP32 nodes, LoRa transport, an SBC-based Go management layer, a notification registry and an event journal with local-network access.

faq.question: How do I start an engineering discussion?
faq.answer: Use the contact form to prepare an email, or email Bora Girgin directly. Include the system, current stage, constraints and the work you need. Scope and availability are discussed before any commitment.

faq.question: What determines pricing and delivery dates?
faq.answer: The agreed scope, technical uncertainty, required deliverables and validation work. There is no fixed public price or guaranteed lead time; these belong in a written proposal.

faq.question: Can I share confidential project information?
faq.answer: Start with a non-confidential summary. Discuss confidentiality arrangements before sharing sensitive files, credentials, schematics or proprietary source code. The website does not provide a file upload service.

faq.question: Where can I inspect the technical work?
faq.answer: Use the interactive hardware explorer and the public repository links. CAD drawings and source code demonstrate the current work; they do not establish physical performance, certification or customer deployment.

faq.question: Is Claude already controlling the hardware?
faq.answer: No. Claude-assisted engineering is planned. Any future command path requires deterministic validation and bounded parameters; local firmware retains real-time control.

faq.question: Does the contact form send my message automatically?
faq.answer: No. It opens your email application with a draft. You review and send that draft there. The website cannot confirm email delivery.
